name: Question 1
problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}$ and ${R}^{2}$, respectively. 

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{2}+{b}_{3}}$ is a basis of ${R}^{3}$
- ${3{c}_{2},{c}_{1}}$ is a basis of ${R}^{2}$
- ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3},x}$ is a basis of ${R}^{3}$
worked_solution:
Since $B$ and $C$ are bases, the following properties must hold:

- $B$ and $C$ are maximally linearly independent sets in ${R}^{2}$ and ${R}^{3},$ respectively, and

- $B$ spans ${R}^{2},$ while $C$ spans ${R}^{3}.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}({b}_{2}+{b}_{3}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+({x}_{2}+{x}_{3}){b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which, since ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ is linearly independent, gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{2}+{b}_{3}}$ spans $V$ since any linear combination of vectors from $B$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{2}+{b}_{3}}:$

$$
{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3}={x}_{1}{b}_{1}+({x}_{2}-{x}_{3}){b}_{2}+{x}_{3}({b}_{2}+{b}_{3})
$$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(3{c}_{2})+{x}_{2}{c}_{1} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}(3{x}_{1}){c}_{2}+{x}_{2}{c}_{1} & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which, since ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ is linearly independent, gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, ${3{c}_{2},{c}_{1}}$ spans $V$ since any linear combination of $C$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ${3{c}_{2},{c}_{1}}:$

$$
{x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}={x}_{1}{c}_{1}+\frac{{x}_{2}}{3}(3{c}_{2})
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ is a basis of ${R}^{3}$, any vector of ${R}^{3},$ including the given vector $x,$ can be written as a linear combination of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2}$ and ${b}_{3}.$ This means that ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3},x}$ is linearly dependent and therefore, cannot be a basis.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
